section_title: Why is Paul so concerned about their devotion to Christ?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that. 2 I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ. 3 I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.

4 For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it very easily. 5 I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.” 6 Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.

context_lines: Paul asks the Corinthians to bear with what he calls a little foolishness. He is about to speak about himself in order to answer people drawing them away from the message he brought. His deeper concern is their faithfulness to Christ.
He pictures the community as a bride promised to one husband. His godly jealousy is a protective concern that they remain devoted to Christ. The picture explains why he takes the threat seriously.

Paul recalls the serpent’s deception of Eve in [Genesis 3:1–6](https://biblehub.com/bsb/genesis/3.htm). He fears a similar deception could turn their minds from simple, pure devotion to Christ. He then names the danger: tolerating another Jesus, a different spirit or a different gospel.

He answers the claims of the people he calls super-apostles by affirming that he is in no way inferior to them. He distinguishes polished speaking from knowledge and reminds the Corinthians that his knowledge has been made clear among them. The message they have received matters as they assess those now teaching them.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand Paul’s jealousy as concern for the church’s faithfulness to Christ. [Wesley’s notes on verses 1–4](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) emphasize devotion directed to Him, while the [USCCB notes on verses 2–4](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/2corinthians/11) connect the marriage picture and Eve’s deception with the danger of accepting a changed gospel.
god_plan_lines: [Ephesians 5:25–32](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/5.htm) explicitly joins the marriage picture with Christ and the church. Christ loves the church, gives Himself for her and works to present her holy and blameless.

That gives Paul’s concern a larger setting. The church belongs to the Lord who has loved and given Himself for her. Faithful teaching serves that relationship by helping people remain devoted to the Christ proclaimed in the gospel.
